It checks input, coordinates the repository interfaces declared in the domain, builds domain entities, hands a state change to the entity (task.markDone()), and maps entities to DTOs. It has no persistence code: no SQL, no ORM and no storage details. It has no transport or framework code: no HTTP status codes, no request or response objects and no routing. The error classes ResourceNotFoundError and InvalidInputError are application-level use-case errors with no transport detail, which suits this layer. A few lines are close to domain territory: the default status "todo" and the check against taskStatuses. Even so, the source of truth for valid statuses stays in the domain (taskStatuses), and checking status values that arrive as input is acceptable at this layer. The state transition itself is left to Task.markDone(). Checking that an assignee exists across aggregates through UserRepository is a typical job for an application service. I found no responsibility that clearly belongs to another kind of layer.
